slices.label: Men outside the South
slices.source: 1850 census (Seventh Census, the first with ages by single year and nativity) aged to November 1852, white men 21+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had largely ended and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Women outside the South
slices.source: No women could vote for president in 1852; women 21+ (1850 census aged to 1852) shown for population only.

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1850 census aged to 1852, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners, most of them enslaved
slices.source: 1850 census aged to 1852, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: 1850 census aged to 1852, foreign-born white men (nativity first recorded in 1850) not yet naturalized; Wisconsin and Michigan let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.

whatIfs.label: Everyone Votes
whatIfs.detail: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
whatIfs.assumption: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1852.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1852 comes out as it did: Pierce wins, 254–42. The closest state was Delaware, which went to Pierce by 0.2 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1850 and 1860 census counts interpolated to 1852 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1852 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

everyone.summary: 8.1 million more adults vote. California, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts and 1 more flip, but Pierce still wins, 281–15. The closest call is Mississippi, which holds for Pierce by 3.0 points. Scott wins in 0 of 100 draws.
assumptions: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1852.
howIGotThis: What changed: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
New voters borrow the behaviour of naturalized citizens of the same state and sex; Black voters outside the South.
The numbers: the 1850 and 1860 census counts interpolated to 1852 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1852 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: I cannot vote myself, but my husband will decide how our household stands tomorrow.
south-white.controlQuote: I cannot vote myself, but my husband will decide how our household stands tomorrow.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: I'll be voting tomorrow for the New England man. These tariffs have been squeezing working folks while the manufacturers grow fat. He'll keep them honest on that score.
men.controlQuote: I'll be voting tomorrow for the New England man. These tariffs have been squeezing working folks while the manufacturers grow fat. He'll keep them honest on that score.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: I cannot vote, being a woman. My husband will cast our household's vote tomorrow, and he favors the general.
women.controlQuote: I cannot vote, being a woman. My husband will cast our household's vote tomorrow, and he favors the general.

questions: Election Day is Tuesday. Can this person vote, how likely are they to vote, and if they vote, for whom?
A neighbour asks what this person will do on Tuesday, 2 November. Will they cast a ballot for president, and for which candidate?
Think about Tuesday's presidential election from where this person stands. How likely are they to vote, and which candidate would get their vote?
